content.value: Primary reading: Machine Learning Systems, Chapter 12. Supplemental: MLCommons MLPerf documentation and benchmark-driven development examples.

This unit teaches students how to measure ML systems without fooling themselves. Benchmarking requires a workload, metrics, environment, protocol, and reproducibility plan. Students distinguish offline model metrics from system metrics such as throughput, tail latency, utilization, power, memory, cost, and failure rate. The unit introduces MLPerf as an example of benchmark discipline and discusses common mistakes: comparing unlike workloads, ignoring warm-up, failing to report variance, and optimizing for benchmark artifacts rather than user outcomes.
Supplemental sources for this unit are listed in the references below. Use them to compare the textbook framing with public talks, documentation, papers, and production guidance.
Studio: design a benchmark for an image classification serving endpoint. Deliverable: workload definition, metrics, environment controls, run protocol, and reporting template.

concepts.name: Benchmark
concepts.description: A standardized task, dataset, or measurement process used to compare systems or models.

concepts.name: Evaluation metric
concepts.description: A quantitative measure used to assess model or system performance.

concepts.name: Baseline model
concepts.description: A simple or established model used as a reference point for comparison.

concepts.name: A/B test
concepts.description: An experiment comparing two variants with live users or traffic to measure outcome differences.

concepts.name: Experiment tracking
concepts.description: Recording configurations, code versions, data versions, metrics, and outputs from experiments.

concepts.name: Reproducibility
concepts.description: The ability to rerun work and obtain the same or meaningfully equivalent results.

concepts.name: Slice evaluation
concepts.description: Evaluating performance on specific subsets of data or users to reveal uneven behavior.

concepts.name: Error analysis
concepts.description: Inspecting failures to understand patterns, causes, and improvement opportunities.
